profiles.name: AWS Knowledge
profiles.description: Search AWS documentation, regional availability and AWS skills. Public and read only.
notes: All five of its tools are declared read only, so they start in Read only.

profiles.name: Cloudflare API
profiles.description: Search and call the whole Cloudflare API, from DNS and Workers to R2 and Zero Trust, in Code Mode.
profiles.signIn: OAuth in your browser, where GateRook signs in with its published client details, or a Cloudflare API token as a Bearer token.
notes: Cloudflare has no read-only switch. Choose Read only on its consent page, or use a read-only API token, to keep execute to reads.
docs and search change nothing, but Cloudflare doesn't declare them read only, so they start in Approval.
With codemode=false in the URL, it lists one tool per API operation, about 3,000, annotated by HTTP method.

tools.reason: It runs JavaScript that can read, create, change or delete anything the sign-in reaches through the Cloudflare API, so GateRook can't tell a read from a change.

profiles.name: DigitalOcean
profiles.description: Droplets, App Platform, Kubernetes, databases, networking and more, with one server per service.

placeholders.name: service
placeholders.description: The service to connect, such as apps, droplets, doks, databases, networking, spaces, functions, volumes, docr, insights, accounts or docs (24 in all).

profiles.signIn: OAuth in your browser, where GateRook registers itself, or a DigitalOcean API token as a Bearer token. The docs service needs no sign-in.
notes: Each service is its own server: add one for each service you use.
DigitalOcean has no read-only switch. A read-only API token keeps its tools to reads.

profiles.name: Vercel
profiles.description: Projects, deployments, build and runtime logs, domains and environment variables on Vercel.
profiles.signIn: OAuth in your browser. Vercel admits only clients it reviewed or that publish their client details, as GateRook does.
notes: Vercel publishes no tool annotations, so this profile names its riskiest tools from Vercel's documentation; the others start as the server declares them.
To limit it to one project, use https://mcp.vercel.com/<team>/<project> instead.
Vercel has no read-only switch: what its tools can change depends on your role in the team.

profiles.name: Firebase
profiles.description: Firestore, Authentication, Hosting, Remote Config, Crashlytics and more through the Firebase CLI.
profiles.signIn: The Firebase CLI's sign-in on this computer (firebase login), or Application Default Credentials.
notes: Firebase has no read-only switch. Add --only with feature names, such as firestore,auth, or --tools with tool names to limit what it lists.
Add --dir with your project's folder to work with its files.
It also lists Google's remote Firestore, Data Connect and Developer Knowledge tools.

tools.reason: It deploys your local project, functions code included.
It runs any GraphQL against your Data Connect service, mutations included.
It runs any GraphQL against the Data Connect emulator.

It returns a download URL that gives anyone who has it the object.

profiles.name: Supabase
profiles.description: Explore the schema, logs, advisors and data of one Supabase project, read only.

placeholders.name: project_ref
placeholders.description: Your project's reference, the ID in its dashboard URL (supabase.com/dashboard/project/<ref>).

pins.purpose: Supabase lists only its read tools, runs SQL read-only, and asks only for read access when you sign in.
pins.missing: Without read_only=true, Supabase also lists the tools that change your project and database, and its sign-in asks for write access. Those tools start in Approval.

pins.purpose: The server reaches this one project, without the tools that list and manage your organizations and projects.
pins.missing: Without project_ref, Supabase's tools reach every project of your account.

profiles.signIn: OAuth in your browser, where GateRook registers itself, or a personal access token as a Bearer token.
notes: With read_only=true Supabase declares execute_sql read only and runs it read-only, so it starts in Read only. Without the switch it starts in Approval.
Supabase leaves out its storage tools unless the URL's features parameter names storage.

tools.reason: It runs DDL that changes your database's schema.
It deploys code as an Edge Function.

profiles.name: Netlify
profiles.description: Projects, deploys, environment variables, forms, extensions and edge traffic on Netlify.

pins.purpose: Netlify lists one tool per operation, so each change, such as renaming a project, gets a mode of its own.
pins.missing: Without verbose=true, Netlify groups its operations: one tool creates projects, changes environment variables, updates forms and deletes form submissions, so they share one mode.

profiles.signIn: OAuth in your browser, where GateRook registers itself, or a Netlify personal access token as a Bearer token.
notes: Netlify has no read-only switch, and its read and write scopes don't limit its tools.

tools.reason: It doesn't deploy: it returns a command that carries a 30-minute token for your Netlify account and asks the agent to run it.
Its deploy-site operation returns a command that carries a 30-minute token for your Netlify account and asks the agent to run it.

profiles.name: Azure DevOps
profiles.description: Work items, repos, pull requests, pipelines, wikis and test plans of one Azure DevOps organization.

placeholders.name: organization
placeholders.description: Your organization, the name in dev.azure.com/<organization>.

profiles.signIn: The Azure CLI's sign-in on this computer (az login). With --authentication pat instead, it takes a personal access token in PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN.
notes: Microsoft's remote server, https://mcp.dev.azure.com/<organization>, admits only an Entra ID app registered in your tenant, which GateRook's sign-in doesn't support yet. This is Microsoft's local server for the same organization.
It has no read-only switch. Add -d with domains, such as core work-items repositories, to limit what it lists.
Tools that ask which project or team to use need it in the call, or ado_mcp_project and ado_mcp_team under Variables: GateRook doesn't pass a server's questions on.

tools.reason: It queues pipeline runs and runs or retries stages, which run your pipelines' code.
It commits file content to a branch, which can change pipeline code and start a build.
It can complete pull requests, and bypass branch policies when asked to.
Despite its read-only declaration, it writes the attachment to a file on this computer when given a path.
